goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:115 — [P1, confidence 100] `if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()))` disables conditional passkeys for every ordinary anonymous login because the helper requires `user != null`, regressing the existing login path while adding re-authentication support.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the code. Looking at the diff, the `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` method in UsernamePasswordForm.java (line 160-162) is defined as `return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. However, the original code at line 113-116 was `if (context.getUser() == null) { if (webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()) { webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context); } }` - this ONLY ran when user was null. The new code at line 115-118 runs `if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()))` which requires user != null. This is actually a CHANGE in behavior - the old code filled the form when user was NULL, the new code fills it when user is NOT null. But looking at the broader context, the code was moved outside the `if (context.getUser() == null)` block, so now it runs regardless of user state. The condition `user != null` in the helper is intentional for the re-authentication case. The finding claims this 'disables conditional passkeys for every ordinary anonymous login' but the original code inside the `if (context.getUser() == null)` block is still being handled - the passkeys form filling just moved to a different condition.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real edge case: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() in UsernamePasswordForm checks if passkeys are enabled at realm level and user is not null, but doesn't verify the user actually has passkey credentials. The test 'reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey' disables passkeys for the entire realm (setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)), so it doesn't test the scenario where passkeys are enabled realm-wide but a specific user has no passkey credentials. This is a legitimate test coverage gap - the code would show passkey UI during re-authentication for users without passkeys when the realm has passkeys enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:294 — [P1, confidence 100] `} catch (Exception nsee) { // expected` converts every Selenium/WebDriver failure in the negative WebAuthn-element check into a passing assertion, so a broken browser session or lookup error falsely passes `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` instead of proving the form is absent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a try-catch block at lines 293-297 that catches generic Exception and treats it as expected behavior. The test intends to verify that the webauthn element is NOT present by expecting a NoSuchElementException. However, catching all Exceptions means any failure (network issues, stale element, browser problems) would be silently swallowed and the test would pass incorrectly. The proper approach would be to catch only NoSuchElementException or use a proper assertion method that checks for element absence. This is a real defect in the test code that could mask actual failures.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new code path `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` added in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java line 53 handles the case when a passkey assertion fails during re-authentication. Looking at the test files in the diff, the new tests (webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication, webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication, etc.) all test successful passkey authentication scenarios during re-authentication. None of the tests actually submit a failing passkey assertion to verify that the new error handling code path works correctly - they test password failures but not passkey failures. This is a legitimate missing test coverage concern for newly added error handling logic.
